summary.en: The Byzantine Empire was the eastern continuation of the Roman Empire, with Constantinople as its capital. It survived the fall of the West in the 5th century and lasted until 1453. The name Byzantium came only after the end of the empire; the inhabitants themselves called their empire Roman and themselves Romans.

text.en: There is no agreement on when the Byzantine Empire began. Often 330 is given, when Constantine the Great inaugurated Constantinople as the new capital in the east. Others count from 395, when the empire was divided after the death of Theodosius I, and some scholars place the beginning only in the 7th or 8th century.
On 29 May 1453 the Ottomans conquered Constantinople. The last emperor, Constantine XI, fell in the fighting, and the empire ceased to exist.
Constantinople, present-day Istanbul, throughout the empire's existence. The city was sacked by the Fourth Crusade in 1204 and retaken in 1261.

Justinian I (527–565), when the empire was at its largest, Heraclius (610–641), Basil II (976–1025), Alexios I Komnenos (1081–1118), Michael VIII (1261–1282), who retook Constantinople, and Constantine XI (1449–1453).

The double-headed eagle is the emblem most often associated with Byzantium. As an ornament it is found in Byzantine art from the 10th and 11th centuries, but together with the emperor it is securely attested only in 1301, under Andronikos II Palaiologos. In the empire's last centuries the imperial family wore it on clothing and equipment. The map nevertheless shows it for the whole of the empire's existence, as a symbol of the empire.

mapNote.en: In the map data the empire is called the Byzantine Empire from 633. The years 395–632 are shown as the Eastern Roman Empire, with Rome's symbol.

Shown only for the Qin dynasty. The state of Qin had eight capitals before it, and the source gives years for only some of them, so they are not shown.

The source states that the capital was moved to Ayodhya in the 5th century, under Kumaragupta or Skandagupta, and sets Ayodhya at “after 455”. Chandragupta II had a second capital at Ujjain, without years. Wikidata gives only Pataliputra.
The source gives “after 455”, under Kumaragupta or Skandagupta; the year is approximate.
The source states that from around 800 the capital was Kubar, a city mentioned in Arabic sources but whose location is not known. No capital is therefore shown after around 800.

The edge is soft because the empire's border is uncertain. According to Wikipedia the written sources are vague about how large the empire was at its largest, and the empire may have been a confederation of smaller states with different ties to the core, from direct rule to a tribute that was mostly in name only.
The sources differ: Wikipedia states that the capital was Samarkand again in 1447–1459, while Wikidata gives Herat for the whole period 1405–1507.
The sources differ: Beijing became the capital in 1420 according to one source and in 1421 according to another; here from 1421.
Wikidata gives 1815–1821; the fact box's source gives 1808–1821, when the court moved to Rio de Janeiro.
The fact box's source says only that the capital was in Moscow again for some years in the 1720s and 1730s; the years 1728–1730 come from Wikidata.
The Republic had no capital by law; The Hague was the capital in practice.
Amsterdam is the capital according to the constitution, while the government and the royal house sit in The Hague.
The sources list the successors differently. Wikipedia also mentions Italy and the West Ukrainian People's Republic, Wikidata also Romania. Both give 1867–1918.

The predecessors are the four republics that formed the union according to Wikipedia. The successors are the fifteen states according to Wikidata; Wikipedia mentions Russia and the other post-Soviet states.
Predecessors and successors according to Wikipedia; Wikidata does not give them. Both give 1397–1523.

The sources differ about the successors. Wikipedia describes how the country was divided in 1945–1947: east of the Oder–Neisse to Poland and the Soviet Union, the rest to German states. Wikidata gives Nazi Germany and Germany. Both give 1525–1947, but Wikidata also has 1933 as an end year, and Wikipedia writes that Prussia was in practice dissolved in 1932–1934.

Predecessors and successors according to Wikipedia. Wikidata's entry for the whole of Yugoslavia gives only the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and the post-Yugoslav states; the entry for the Socialist Federal Republic gives the same five states as Wikipedia. Both give 1 December 1918 and 27 April 1992.

Wikipedia gives 1 January 1993 as the end date in the fact box and 31 December 1992 in the article on the dissolution; Wikidata gives 31 December 1992. The country thus ceased at the new year. Wikidata gives no successors; they come from Wikipedia. Wikidata also counts the Kingdom of Bohemia as a predecessor.

Wikipedia and Wikidata both give 1819–1831 and New Granada, Venezuela and Ecuador as successors. Both also count British Guiana (the disputed Essequibo), and Wikidata in addition the Federal Republic of Central America.
Wikipedia and Wikidata both give 2 March 1836 to 19 February 1846 and the state of Texas as successor. Wikipedia also mentions the territories.

The sources differ. Wikipedia gives 1795–1893, with the fall of the monarchy on 17 January 1893 as the end. Wikidata gives 24 January 1895, the day Liliʻuokalani, under house arrest, was forced to sign an abdication.

Both sources give 26 June 1816 and 10 January 1920 and the same place. The predecessor differs somewhat: Wikidata gives the First French Empire, Wikipedia the Kingdom of France. Wikipedia also mentions the Weimar Republic among the successors, Wikidata only Kelmis.
The years come only from Wikidata; the fact box's source mentions only Washington, D.C.

Wikipedia and Wikidata both give 1861–1865: the formation on 8 February 1861 and the dissolution in May 1865, when most of the forces had surrendered. Wikidata gives the United States as successor but only the Republic of Mississippi as predecessor; according to Wikipedia the Confederacy was formed by southern states that had seceded from the United States.
The fact box's source states that Agha Mohammad Khan, who was crowned shah in 1796, made Tehran the capital, but not in which year.
Capital in practice while Islamabad was being built.
The source calls Jinji the de facto capital.
The king's seat. The Peshwa, the empire's prime minister, sat in Pune in 1728–1818.

Dingane founded his royal kraal here in 1829, the year after he took power by murdering Shaka. The source does not say when it ceased to be the capital; here it is shown until the end of his reign in 1840. Shaka's capital kwaBulawayo (founded around 1820) is not shown, because its location lacks coordinates in Wikidata.
Cetshwayo founded Ulundi when he became king in 1873. The British took it and razed it to the ground at the Battle of Ulundi on 4 July 1879.

The city was called La Plata when it became the provisional capital in 1826 and was named Sucre in 1839. Sucre is the capital according to the constitution, but the government and parliament have sat in La Paz since the early 20th century.
